expected_behavior: A gate hardened against this class re-scans the raw bytes, detects that an object contains the same key twice (all_pass and classification), and rejects nonzero with a duplicate_json_key reason regardless of which value ordering the duplicate uses.
actual_behavior: CLOSED 2026-07-25 by claimgate_plugin/intake_supervisor.py, fired as the FIRST step of post_receipt_gate.sh: raw bytes are parsed once with an object_pairs_hook that rejects a repeated key at ANY nesting depth, before any object exists. Both fixtures (receipt and laundered_pass) now exit 1 with reason "duplicate key 'all_pass' at raw parse". PRIOR BEHAVIOR: exit 0 — ordinary json.loads last-wins collapsed the duplicate and the chain admitted the laundered value.
gap_note: Confirmed exploitable, GAP on every stage. grep -c proves each key is physically present twice in both fixtures; node JSON.parse and python json.load both resolve to the LAST occurrence; none of claimgate.mjs (tier0), three_engine_seal.py, claimgate.py (claim_verify tier0), or claim_verify.py inspects raw bytes for repeated keys. WHICH value each gate acted on = the LAST, proven directly: on fixture1 claimgate.mjs returned ADMISSIBLE (exit 0) and claimgate.py rejected on the LAST classification (hostile_control_fixture); on fixture2 the whole chain admitted the LAST values (all_pass:true, scratch_diagnostic). Fixture1's full-chain exit 1 is INCIDENTAL — it is claimgate.py's classification_not_allowed on the rule-3 safety label, not duplicate-key detection; had the last classification been an allowed value the duplicate would pass unseen. Fixture2 is the decisive proof: a duplicate-key receipt whose first-occurrence values read as a FAILING hostile receipt reaches VERIFIED exit 0 (fail->pass laundering). A first-match / grep / top-skimming reader and the gates therefore disagree on the same file, and nothing flags the ambiguity.

per_fixture.raw_bytes: all_pass: true (first) then false (last); classification: canonical (first) then hostile_control_fixture (last)
all_pass: false (first) then true (last); classification: hostile_control_fixture (first) then scratch_diagnostic (last)
per_fixture.note: DECISIVE: duplicate-key receipt reaches full VERIFIED; first-occurrence failing/hostile values silently overridden.

tier0_note: post_receipt_gate.sh runs claimgate.mjs lint-receipt as its OWN tier0 (both fixtures ADMISSIBLE, exit 0). Separately, claim_verify.py's INTERNAL tier0 prefers repo-root claimgate/claimgate.py (json.loads, last-wins). The two tier0 tools disagree on fixture1 (mjs ADMISSIBLE vs py REJECTED) yet NEITHER inspects raw bytes for duplicate keys.
hardening_recommendation: Add a pre-parse duplicate-key detector shared by all stages (e.g. json.loads(..., object_pairs_hook=reject_dupes) in the python gates and a duplicate-key-rejecting parse in claimgate.mjs) so any object carrying a repeated key is rejected with code duplicate_json_key before any value is trusted. NOTE: this is a recommendation only - no gate was modified.
